 Acura ZDX Recall: 14,648 EVs May Dump Brake Pressure
 by 
 TTAC News Staff 
 (IC: ) 
 Published:  November 14th, 2026 
 Share 
 The ZDX has a problem that strikes at the one job a brake system has. American Honda Motor Co. is recalling 14,648 units of the 2024 Acura ZDX, all of them all-wheel-drive models, over a software error that can dump brake pressure without the driver asking for it.
 Enjoy our posts? 
 Add TheTruthAboutCars as a Preferred Source on Google 
 The defect lives in the electronic brake control module. According to the NHTSA recall filing, faulty software may trigger the anti-lock braking system without warning and bleed off brake pressure. Translated out of regulatory language: the car can decide, on its own, to let go of the brakes mid-stop.
 NHTSA's paperwork is blunt about the stakes. "A loss of brake pressure may reduce braking ability, extending the distance needed to stop and increasing the risk of a crash." For an electric crossover, longer stopping distances are not a rounding error.
 The remedy is a software update to the electronic brake control module, delivered either over-the-air or at a dealer, free of charge. The OTA option spares owners a service appointment, which is the one modern convenience that makes a brake recall slightly less of a chore.
 Acura expects to mail owner notification letters starting December 14, 2026. Owners with questions can reach Acura customer service at 1-800-382-2238. Acura's internal number for the campaign is CQC, and the NHTSA campaign number is 26V735000.
 This is not the ZDX's first trip to the recall page for this issue. Per NHTSA, campaign 26V735000 expands previous recall number 24V614, which means Acura is widening the net on a brake-pressure problem it already addressed once. Expansions happen when the original remedy or population turns out to be incomplete, and a second pass at the braking software is not a reassuring look.
 A brake recall that needs a second attempt does the nameplate no favors.
